channel.title: Dumb Game Lab Blog
channel.description: Korean everyday places, cozy idle tycoons, and notes from a tiny game studio in Seoul.

item.title: 9 Squishy and Slime Apps: What Gets in the Way Before You Touch
item.description: We opened 9 squishy and slime game apps on a Samsung Galaxy Z Flip5, two of them Korean mallangi apps. Birth-year windows, full-screen ads and 5-minute touch blocks: what gets in the way before you touch, as of November 21, 2026.

item.title: There's a reason this caterpillar flings poop
item.description: One leaf-sheltering caterpillar flings its poop away. The smell can guide hunting wasps to it, so removing the clue can reduce the risk of discovery.

item.title: We ran 9 Android ASMR games on a real phone
item.description: We installed nine ASMR games on a Samsung Galaxy Z Flip5 and relaunched each in airplane mode. Install size, first screen and whether an ad blocks the game, checked on 20 November 2026.

item.title: Why Koreans Go to a PC Bang for Concert Ticketing
item.description: Why Koreans pack PC bangs (Korean internet cafes) on concert ticketing day, and what the sources actually back up. Queue numbers, the NOL (Interpark) captcha on a Korean keyboard, prepaid kiosks and Korean phone verification for foreign fans.

item.title: This airport waits for the tide to go out
item.description: Barra Airport in Scotland uses a beach as its runway. Scheduled flights follow the tides. Once the airport closes and the windsock is down, people can walk on the beach.

item.title: What's on the shelf at a Korean neighborhood bakery
item.description: The Korean bakery items you will see on almost every neighborhood shelf: red bean bun, soboro bread, cream bun, salt bread and kkwabaegi. What each one looks like, what is inside, and how a bakery grows, with screens from our game.

item.title: Dessert disguised itself as asparagus
item.description: Historical ice cream molds made shapes such as asparagus and fish. This is a story about vegetable shapes, not confirmed vegetable flavors.

item.title: I wasted 25% of a day's tokens, and 14.4% went to rewarming the cache
item.description: A solo game dev's daily Claude Code token usage log. 22.7M of 90.6M tokens (25%) went to waste, and the biggest bucket was cache rewarming at 13.0M (14.4%). The cause, how prompt caching is priced, and what I changed.

item.title: Twelve squelch sounds lost to my old honey sound. Then I actually listened to it.
item.description: I tested 12 squelch candidates for the honey level of my ASMR climbing game. The old sound won on score, then turned out to be a drum hit. So I swapped in one Freesound CC0 recording, cut into 10 variations with no processing.

item.title: One glove becomes two for this crab
item.description: In an experiment with one species of boxer crab, crabs split a remaining anemone after losing the other. The two pieces regenerated over several days.

item.title: Where Korean salt bread really comes from: Japan's shio pan vs the Korean version
item.description: Salt bread started in a small Ehime bakery in Japan around 2003 and took off in Korea around 2021. Why it is hollow, how it differs from a croissant, calories and prices, with sources.

item.title: This book hides a picture in its edges
item.description: Some books hide paintings on their page edges. Fanning the pages reveals them, and some books show a different picture in each direction.

item.title: We Tried 8 Slime Simulator Apps on a Real Phone
item.description: We opened 8 slime simulator apps on a Samsung Galaxy Z Flip5 and relaunched them in airplane mode. Install tiers and ad labels checked on Google Play, Nov 16, 2026.

item.title: Deliver the mail. Now catch the boat!
item.description: On Geneva Lake in Wisconsin, summer mail carriers jump between docks and a moving boat. If they miss the return jump, the captain comes back for them.

item.title: When do hit mobile games show their first ad? We timed 8 of them
item.description: First-ad timing in 8 popular mobile games, measured on a phone: when the first ad showed up, what kind it was, and whether you could skip it. Plus what we copied into our own games.

item.title: Galaxy Store Rejected My Game Because the Default Language Wasn't English
item.description: My first Samsung Galaxy Store submission came back as Test Confirmation Rejected. The app was fine. The default language was set to Korean instead of English. Here is what the report said and how I fixed it.

item.title: ASMR Tower Roblox on Your Phone: Two Ways to Play
item.description: How to play a Roblox ASMR tower on your phone. The Roblox app route, and Wakppu Tower, a separate Android ASMR jump game with 8 maps. Controls, ads and what happens when you fall.

item.title: Food's over there. This bee rolls a ball.
item.description: Bumblebees repeatedly rolled small balls without a food reward. Researchers found that the behavior met criteria for animal play.

item.title: 122 of 165 New Tickets Were the Same Check
item.description: 165 new tickets opened in one day, and 122 of them came from a single screen check tool. Text and button overlap alone was 101. Here are the numbers from the day the backlog went from 278 to 412, and where I was wrong to answer it with one more ticket.

item.title: Zipper Started as a Name for Boots
item.description: Zipper was originally a name for rubber boots in 1923. The fastener ended up taking the name.

item.title: I Closed 78 Tickets and the Backlog Stayed the Same
item.description: I spent a whole day closing tickets as a solo developer, and the backlog ended the day the same size. I closed 78 and 101 new ones opened. Here are the numbers, and where I was wrong to treat closed tickets as work done.

item.title: "Eorin Baekseong" Did Not Mean Children
item.description: In the 15th century "eorida" meant foolish. The sense of "young" appeared from the 16th century and is the main meaning today.

item.title: The Day I Reported Fixing the Same 16 Bugs Twice
item.description: I opened the tickets my crash collector created and all 16 were bugs I had already fixed. Old app versions that never updated kept sending crashes that looked new. Here is where my call was wrong and the order I filter them in now.

item.title: Bubble Wrap Started Out as Wallpaper
item.description: In 1957 two engineers sealed shower curtains together to trap air bubbles. They failed to sell it as wallpaper before it found its place as packaging.

item.title: We Got 1,269 Views and Not a Single Install
item.description: We posted promo shorts for a spinning wheel app in two formats, app screen recording (A) and character animation (B). Seven days later the views were 681 vs 588, and installs that reached the store were 0 for both. Here are the numbers and the limits.

item.title: In England You Paid Tax on Every Window
item.description: England introduced a tax based on the number of windows in 1696 and repealed it in 1851. Houses with windows blocked to avoid it still survive.

item.title: One Alarm Used 5 Million Rows of the Daily Read Limit on Its Own: Tracing Durable Objects Error 1101
item.description: One alarm in my game server read 4.98 million rows of the free Durable Objects limit (5 million rows read per day), and my error collector went down with error 1101 too. Here is how I traced it and fixed it with indexes, a cache, and monitoring.

item.title: There's No Cat in Catgut
item.description: Despite its name, catgut has never been documented as made from cats. It came mostly from sheep or goat intestines, and some players still use it.

item.title: I Got the Same Feedback 20 Times. Writing Rules Twice Changed Nothing
item.description: Every time I showed a game screen, the feedback was "this looks rushed." Writing rules twice didn't help, so I changed the order: score it side by side with the reference screen before anyone sees it. Here is the log.

item.title: Yesterday Island and Tomorrow Island Are Under 4 km Apart
item.description: Russia's Big Diomede and the US's Little Diomede are 3.8 km apart, yet the date line runs between them and clocks differ by 21 hours.
